candidates.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
candidates.content: Recent work shows that multimodal agents increasingly self-improve without recurring human annotation. However, each self-improvement mechanism is designed and evaluated within a single scenario, leaving its preconditions unverified under cross-scenario transfer. This survey investigates the structural source of asymmetric mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, multimodal generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation. We first formalize the self-evolving multimodal agent by four criteria and a differentia of self-reference, and adopt the three-stage self-evolving loop of experience generation, feedback acquisition, and update consolidation as our analytical framework to position the scenarios along ceilings on rollout count and feedback fidelity. Comparing self-evolving with fixed loops within each scenario separates the limitations that the scenario imposes from those inherent in the self-evolving design. candidates.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
candidates.content: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions. More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer poorly

This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap , the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub .) candidates.title: datasette 1.0a43
candidates.content: Release: datasette 1.0a43 I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone , which is now 53% complete. The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method. There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory : private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed). There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0 . A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai , Peter Olkhovets , Ilya Khalafi , and Ankita Advitot . The feature I'm most excited about is a pretty tiny one: I've added CSS multi-page view transitions to Datasette!

candidates.title: The Narrative Gap: Can LLMs Help Us Navigate Diverse Narratives Across Languages?
candidates.content: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people seek and consume information, including accounts that differ across languages and regions, especially on contested topics. Supporting diverse information seeking requires models to help users navigate competing narratives across languages and information streams. We define six capabilities necessary for diverse multilingual information seeking: three foundational capabilities for narrative inclusion, narrative exclusion, and missing narrative identification; and three higher-level capabilities for presenting diverse narratives, preserving narrative coverage under confirmatory queries, and maintaining information parity across languages. To guide the development of those information seeking capabilities, we introduce NarrativeBench, a benchmark comprising 1,333 news articles in 23 publication languages across 23 contested topics and 460 Reddit-grounded queries. Evaluating 14 LLMs across 24 query languages, we find that current models lack the capabilities needed to reliably navigate diverse narratives, limiting users' control over the perspectives they receive and leaving substantial gaps in exposure to competing accounts

This phase II trial studies the effect of lenalidomide and vaccine in treating patients with early-stage asymptomatic chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma. Lenalidomide may stop the growth of cancer cells by blocking blood flow to the cancer. It may also stimulate the immune system in different ways and stop cancer cells from growing. candidates.title: Glomerular Filtration Rates and Risk of Adverse Health Outcomes
candidates.content: To the Editor A recent study reported the association of adverse health outcomes with measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR) and estimated GFR (eGFR) calculated with plasma creatinine, cystatin C, or both. The authors concluded that their findings support the current GFR thresholds by showing that, compared with a GFR of 90 mL/min/1.73 m2, adverse outcomes were increased at GFR levels of 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. In the accompanying Editorial, Dr Potluri and colleagues stated that “these results reinforce that all contemporary approaches to assessing kidney filtration function are imperfect and should motivate clinicians to adopt a contextual approach that recognizes clinical scenarios in which creatinine-based assessments should be viewed with skepticism and additional testing would be beneficial” and that “many patients could benefit from a more convenient approach to directly measuring GFR.”

candidates.title: End-of-Life Care for People Who Are Incarcerated—Reply
candidates.content: In Reply We appreciate the response to our article by Ms Ofori-Darko and Dr McClelland and agree wholeheartedly that the definition of palliative care for incarcerated patients should be comprehensive and match the community standard. This standard includes all evidence-based interventions that palliate symptoms during serious, life-limiting illness. We also agree that short-course or single-fraction regimens of radiation therapy may be indicated for incarcerated patients with serious illness who may face additional barriers to longer-duration treatments. Other palliative treatments may also include some forms of chemotherapy, immunotherapy, antibiotics, blood transfusions, and diuresis. Some treatments may lose palliative effectiveness over time and thus be stopped as a person transitions to hospice care.

candidates.title: Intravenous Vitamin C and Mortality and Organ Dysfunction in Severe Burn Injury
candidates.content: To the Editor We read with interest the article from the recent VICTORY trial that reported increased mortality in patients with severe burns who were randomized to 4-day administration of vitamin C vs placebo. The rationale for vitamin C administration was the massive release of oxygen free radicals following severe burns. However, the median time to discharge alive from the intensive care unit was 42.5 days in the placebo group, suggesting that a 4-day course of vitamin C may have been too short to affect outcomes. Notably, 2 previous randomized clinical trials in critically ill patients reported that abrupt discontinuation of a 4-day course of vitamin C was associated with increased mortality.

candidates.title: Granzyme K-expressing CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells, complement activation and histotoxic immunity
candidates.content: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01364-5 This Perspective discusses the emerging biology of a unique population of granzyme K-expressing CD8+ T cells. Unlike canonical cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, which mediate direct cell killing, granzyme K-expressing CD8+ T cells activate the complement cascade and promote localized tissue inflammation. The authors propose that such ‘tissue histotoxicity’ is an important defence strategy, allowing CD8+ T cells to target a tissue neighbourhood instead of one cell at a time.

candidates.title: [Correspondence] The Perth Declaration to eliminate rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease
candidates.content: The persistence of rheumatic heart disease reveals how profoundly social inequity can shape who benefits from medical progress. Approximately 55 million people live with the disease, and more than 370 000 die each year.1 It is the most common acquired heart disease in people younger than 25 years, occurring during the years in which these individuals finish their education, form families, and build working lives. Rheumatic heart disease affects women and girls in greater numbers than men and boys,1 and their needs have too often been overlooked.

candidates.title: An RNA-targeting ADP-ribosyltransferase toxin uncouples mRNA stability from productive translation
candidates.content: Abstract Messenger RNA (mRNA) modifications regulate transcript stability and translation efficiency across diverse biological systems, but the consequences of toxin-mediated mRNA modification in bacteria remain poorly understood. RhsP2 was recently identified as an RNA-targeting interbacterial ADP-ribosyltransferase toxin, but whether mRNAs are physiological substrates remained unknown. Here, we show that RhsP2 targets mRNA coding sequences and in doing so prevents their efficient translation. eCLIP-seq reveals preferential association of RhsP2 with UAAG-enriched motifs, and biochemical analyses showed that these sequences are preferred substrates for ribose 2′-OH ADP-ribosylation. Unexpectedly, modified mRNAs were broadly stabilized despite impaired protein synthesis, demonstrating that RhsP2 uncouples transcript stability from productive translation. Monosome- and disome-seq analyses show that RhsP2-modified mRNAs induce ribosome stalling and collision, and in vitro translation reactions demonstrate that ADP-ribosylation of mRNAs is sufficient to block translation elongation. Together, these findings establish mRNA ADP-ribosylation as a mechanism of toxin-mediated translational

candidates.title: Self-organized criticality in a mammalian RNA-interference circuit
candidates.content: Living systems have been argued to operate near critical points, but their relevance at the cellular level is poorly understood. Critical states allow for a high sensitivity to external inputs and maximal information transfer and display fluctuations at all scales. Critical points are very special, and require the fine tuning of a control parameter, which is hard to reconcile with the robustness of living cells. Self-organized criticality (SOC) proposes that feedback, rather than tuning, brings a system to its critical point. Here we show that RNA interference, in which messenger RNAs compete for shared silencing machinery and so queue for service, together with negative feedback gives rise to SOC in mammalian cells. In a synthetic circuit, a protein repressor whose mRNA competes with the mRNA of a fluorescent reporter that it represses senses the congestion of the queue, closing the feedback loop. Theory and stochastic simulations show that the loop holds the queue near its critical point despite changes in its parameters, and that expression becomes intermittent, with scale-free bursts. candidates.title: Associative Learning and Memory Erasure in a Synthetic Multicellular System
candidates.content: Learning is a basic form of adaptation that organisms display from neural systems to single cells. In associative learning, the pairing of two stimuli lets one of them evoke the response to the other. Engineering this behavior in a living cell is difficult, because coincidence detection, memory, and conditional readout must be wired into a single regulatory network. Here we build a consortium of five E. coli strains that distributes the operations of associative learning and communicates through one diffusible quorum-sensing signal. The same signal acts as the memory trace. One strain detects the coincidence of the two inputs, a second maintains the memory through positive feedback in the shared medium, a third reads it out on the conditioned stimulus, a fourth reports the unconditioned response, and a fifth erases the memory on command. We show experimentally that the assembled consortium learns the association, since a stimulus that is silent before training evokes a strong response after pairing. candidates.title: Rab27a modulation reverses hemorrhage-induced neutrophil dysfunction in response to secondary respiratory challenge
candidates.content: Patients recovering from hemorrhage are susceptible to secondary respiratory infections, owing to dysregulated innate immune responses. Using a two-hit mouse model of hemorrhage followed by a secondary respiratory challenge with Staphylococcus aureus or lipopolysaccharide (LPS), we investigated the role of Rab27a in the neutrophil response to pulmonary inflammation and host defense. Hemorrhage followed by S. aureus infection increased surface CD63 expression on pulmonary neutrophils, indicating azurophilic granule release, and was accompanied by reduced neutrophil entry into the airspaces of the lung. Using HoxB8-conditional neutrophil progenitor (NP) transplantation to neutrophil chimeric mice, we observe that Rab27a-deficient neutrophils have enhanced recruitment into the extravascular pulmonary compartment compared with wild-type (WT) neutrophils. Furthermore, pharmacological intervention with Nexinhib20, a small-molecule inhibitor of Rab27a-JFC1 interactions, attenuated systemic and pulmonary inflammatory responses in the two-hit model, including a reduction in circulating myeloperoxidase (MPO) levels. candidates.title: The antagonism of sex chromosomes and sex hormones dictates outcomes in Th17 cell-mediated central nervous system autoimmunity.
candidates.content: Biological sex traits are shaped by the combined effects of both sex hormones and chromosomes. How these factors interact in sex-related autoimmune diseases, such as multiple sclerosis (MS), has been a subject of intense recent interest. Here, using the Four Core Genotype (FCG) mouse model, in which these two variables can be disentangled, we describe an antagonism between sex hormones and chromosomes that potently influences outcomes in T helper 17 (Th17)-driven progressive central nervous system (CNS) autoimmunity. Male gonadal hormones dampen disease severity, irrespective of sex chromosome complement, by promoting a Wnt/{beta}-catenin signaling program associated with a homeostatic, non-pathogenic Th17 phenotype. By contrast, XY chromosomal complement exacerbates Th17 pathogenicity in a recipient sex-dependent manner; we identify the X-linked molecule SUV39H1 as an inhibitor of inflammatory Th17 cell function. Unexpectedly, we found that hormonally and chromosomally female FCG Th17 cells induced far more severe disease than WT female counterparts despite being genetically identical, pointing to a parental imprinting effect in dictating Th17 cell pathogenicity. candidates.title: Impact of DENV-ZIKV cross-reactivity in Southeast Asia: A modelling study in Thailand
candidates.content: Dengue virus (DENV) is endemic across Southeast Asia (SEA), where a large proportion of adults have been infected. Zika virus (ZIKV) has circulated in the region for decades but the extent of transmission remains unclear. Prior infection with one virus can protect against or enhance infection with the other, but the population-level consequences are unknown. We developed an age-structured DENV-ZIKV model with nine cross-reactivity assumptions combining cross-protection and subsequent enhancement, and simulated sustained co-circulation under changing Thai demography. Through cross-reactivity, DENV strongly shaped ZIKV transmission, whereas ZIKV had little effect on DENV transmission. Under cross-protection, ZIKV transmission occurred as infrequent outbreaks without changes in long-term ZIKV burden. When prior DENV infection enhanced both ZIKV infection and symptomatic risk, this burden roughly doubled. Population ageing raised the mean age of DENV and ZIKV cases by over 20 years, more than cross-reactivity did. candidates.content: BackgroundMalaria transmission in Senegal is seasonal and spatially heterogeneous, but the consistency of dynamical malaria models with routine surveillance has rarely been tested with monthly subnational data. MethodsWe analysed monthly confirmed cases from the National Malaria Control Programme (PNLP) regional database (14 regions, 2009-2025) and reports of the 79 health districts (2016-2025). Ten bias-adjusted NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 models (1995-2014; SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 to 2100) were evaluated against CHIRPS rainfall; VECTRI was driven by MRI-ESM2-0, the model closest to the ensemble median change. ResultsNational incidence averaged 24.5 cases per 1,000 per year without trend over 2009-2024, but increased in Kedougou, Kolda and Tambacounda, which reported 58.7 % of cases for 11.3 % of the population. The test positivity rate (TPR) decreased from 22.5 % in 2016 to 16.2 % in 2024.
